name: stri_startswith_charclass
title: Determine if the Start or End of a String Matches a Pattern

origin.description: Report whether the code point at from belongs to a character class.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: Character vector of strings to test.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: An ICU UnicodeSet pattern: \p{L}, \p{N}, \p{WhiteSpace}, [:WhiteSpace:], or [a-z]. A bare name such as WhiteSpace, and \w, are not patterns. An empty pattern is an error.

arguments.name: from
arguments.text: 1-based code-point index. Negative values count back from the end. -1 is the last code point.

arguments.name: negate
arguments.text: If TRUE, report the opposite answer.

origin.details: Only one code point is tested. The index just past the last code point reads the C string's trailing NUL, so an empty string tests U+0000. A class that contains U+0000 therefore matches at that position. A missing string, pattern, or from is NA.
origin.example:
x <- stri_startswith_charclass(" trim", "\\p{Z}")
sentence <- paste0('stri_startswith_charclass(" trim", "\\p{Z}") returns ', ifelse(x, "TRUE", "FALSE"), '.')
writeLines(sentence)

translation.description: Report whether the code point at from_ belongs to a character class.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: String, missing value, or list of those.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: An ICU UnicodeSet pattern: \p{L}, \p{N}, \p{WhiteSpace}, [:WhiteSpace:], or [a-z]. A bare name such as WhiteSpace, and \w, are not patterns. An empty pattern is an error. Membership is ICU 76, Unicode 16.

arguments.name: from_
arguments.text: R's from. A 1-based code-point index. Negative values count back from the end. -1 is the last code point.

arguments.name: negate
arguments.text: If true, report the opposite answer.

translation.details: Only one code point is tested. The index just past the last code point tests U+0000, because the installed function reads the C string's trailing NUL. An empty string therefore tests U+0000. A missing string, pattern, or from_ is NA.
translation.value: A list of bools. A missing result is NA.
translation.example:
from stringi.charclass import stri_startswith_charclass
x = stri_startswith_charclass(" trim", "\\p{Z}")
sentence = f'stri_startswith_charclass(" trim", "\\p{{Z}}") returns {"TRUE" if x[0] else "FALSE"}.'
print(sentence)
